claims.text: Trazodone CI: an MAOI now or within 14 days, including linezolid or IV methylene blue (serotonin syndrome risk);
claims.quote: Patients taking, or within 14 days of stopping, monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), including MAOIs such as linezolid or intravenous methylene blue, because of an increased risk of serotonin syndrome

claims.text: wait at least 14 days after stopping trazodone before an MAOI.
claims.quote: At least 14 days must elapse between discontinuation of a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) antidepressant and initiation of trazodone hydrochloride tablets. In addition, at least 14 days must elapse after stopping trazodone hydrochloride tablets before starting an MAOI antidepressant
claims.locator: 2.4 Switching to or from Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitor Antidepressant

claims.text: Priapism (painful erections over 6 hours) has been reported and can cause irreversible damage if not treated promptly.
claims.quote: Cases of priapism (painful erections greater than 6 hours in duration) have been reported in men receiving trazodone. Priapism, if not treated promptly, can result in irreversible damage to the erectile tissue.

claims.text: Prolongs the QT/QTc interval: avoid with known QT prolongation, CYP3A4 inhibitors or other QT-prolonging drugs.
claims.quote: Trazodone prolongs the QT/QTc interval. The use of trazodone should be avoided in patients with known QT prolongation or in combination with other drugs that are inhibitors of CYP3A4 (e.g., itraconazole, clarithromycin, voriconazole), or known to prolong QT interval

claims.text: Serotonin syndrome risk rises with other serotonergic drugs (eg, SSRIs, SNRIs, triptans).
claims.quote: Serotonin Syndrome: Increased risk when co-administered with other serotonergic agents (e.g., SSRI, SNRI, triptans)

claims.text: Aspirin, NSAIDs, other antiplatelets, warfarin and other anticoagulants may add to bleeding risk; with warfarin, monitor coagulation indices when starting, changing or stopping trazodone.
claims.quote: Concomitant use of aspirin, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS), other antiplatelet drugs, warfarin, and other anticoagulants may add to this risk. Case reports and epidemiological studies (case-control and cohort design) have demonstrated an association between use of drugs that interfere with serotonin reuptake and the occurrence of gastrointestinal bleeding. Bleeding events related to drugs that interfere with serotonin reuptake have ranged from ecchymosis, hematoma, epistaxis, and petechiae to life-threatening hemorrhages. Inform patients about the risk of bleeding associated with the concomitant use of trazodone and antiplatelet agents or anticoagulants. For patients taking warfarin, carefully monitor coagulation indices when initiating, titrating, or discontinuing trazodone.
